text: The Herman Skolnik Award is given each year by the Division of Chemical Information of the American Chemical Society to honor exceptional contributions to both the theory and practice of chemical information science. As of 2024[update], the award includes a cash prize of 3,000 US dollars.[1] The award is named after Herman Skolnik (1914–1994), who co-founded the ACS Division of Chemical Literature in 1948 and played a significant role in the division's development.[2] Herman Skolnik was the first recipient of the award.
